items.requirement: Inventory current low-level call sites across application and library code: parameters, ranges, guards, indices, arrays, packing, hierarchy, recursion, clocks, callbacks and naming.
Create minimal compile probes for the desired ordinary syntax before declaring any feature unsupported; distinguish existing syntax, wrapper-only improvements and compiler gaps.
Specify three distinct conditions: concrete Scala `Boolean` selects during elaboration; parameter-only conditions generate HDL branches; hardware `Bool` uses runtime `when` logic.
Define handling of Scala `if` requiring `Boolean`: select a compiler rewrite/typed staging design that does not coerce symbolic conditions to a concrete witness value.
Specify symbolic equality/comparison syntax, including `==` versus `===`, so host object equality cannot silently choose a branch.
Specify the supported staged Scala subset, expression-valued branches, helper-method boundaries and restrictions on side effects, mutation and early return.
Keep ordinary concrete loops compatible; document explicit intent where a concrete loop must be retained as a generate loop.
Map new work to existing CA evidence without marking historical bug fixes incomplete; use new issue IDs only for demonstrated new gaps.
Choose one concise typed declaration for integer/Boolean HDL parameters, including HDL name, default, legal domain and dependent constraints.
Infer forwarding from constructor arguments and named bindings; remove user-maintained positional formal vectors and `.toElabInt` plumbing from normal code.
Preserve symbolic arithmetic for widths, depths, counts, slices, logarithms and derived local constants through helper methods and named intermediates.
Distinguish HDL parameters from Scala specialization arguments such as payload type and operation callback; do not turn hardware registers into parameters.
Provide clear overflow, signedness, zero-width and illegal-domain diagnostics at the authored expression.
Retain optional simulation-only parameter checks and the current configurable cleanup policy for `ifndef SYNTHESIS` blocks.
Lower parameter-dependent `if`/`else if`/`else` to generate branches using existing branch-domain proofs.
Support nested guards and guards inside finite loops without manual source labels or `ElabBool` control calls.
Preserve declaration/assignment ownership and branch-local child visibility; hoist only when scope and driver ownership remain valid.
Reject runtime hardware conditions used as elaboration guards with an actionable diagnostic directing users to `when`.
Diagnose incomplete combinational assignments, illegal cross-branch references and conflicting drivers without falsely treating mutually exclusive branches as multiple drivers.
Support `for (i <- 0 until count)` with symbolic finite bounds and a retained HDL `genvar`.
Support nested loops and multidimensional arrays; preserve row/column structure rather than flattening through bit arithmetic.
Define supported `to`, non-unit step and reverse ranges; implement them or reject explicitly rather than silently unrolling.
Support ordinary affine reads/writes such as `lanes(2*i)`, `lanes(2*i+1)` and `terms(counter)(port)`.
Carry guarded bounds proofs from `if (2*i+1 < count)` into both reads and writes, including odd counts and singleton base cases.
Prove write coverage, non-overlap and legal index domains; retain negative tests for out-of-bounds and overlapping accesses.
Allow operation callbacks and helper functions in loop bodies while retaining symbolic-index ownership.
Preserve a single authored loop containing combine, pipeline and packing statements when their scopes permit it; do not require a separate loop for each assignment.
Add optional loop labels and stable automatically derived names without exposing compiler-internal source tags.
Define a documented representation policy for internal `Vec`, nested `Vec`, packed vectors, unpacked array ports and arrays of bundles.
Preserve element widths, dimensions and signedness as symbolic type information through declaration, indexing, assignment and child connections.
Offer direct aggregate ports and connections where the selected HDL dialect supports them; provide a documented packed boundary for Verilog targets that cannot express unpacked ports.
Support whole-array and whole-word assignment without duplicate scalar `combined_1` signals plus array views.
Support ordinary word slices such as `bits(i * width, width bits)` with automatic correlation proofs for symbolic stride and width.
Make `asBits` / `assignFromBits` or a concise typed word-view API preserve least-significant-lane-first ordering, signed values and multidimensional ordering.
Emit word-level packing/unpacking generate loops rather than bit-level division/modulo loops or giant concatenations.
Preserve combinational constant drivers as continuous/combinational assignments, never initialization-only `initial` blocks.
Avoid packed-view/carrier/result chains unless a real type/ownership boundary requires them; make unavoidable plumbing anonymous compiler temporaries.
Cover dynamic hardware indexing separately from symbolic generate indexing, including read muxes, write decoding and out-of-range policy.
Preserve explicit memory semantics: do not turn register arrays into RAMs or change read latency/reset behavior as a syntax transformation.
Recognize guarded direct self-construction using `new SameComponent(nextCount, ...)` without executing an unbounded chain of Scala constructors.
Infer the recursive boundary, typed ports and named parameter forwarding from the component declaration and call site.
Emit a self-instance of one shared operation-specialized HDL definition, with branch-local connections and legal decreasing parameter bindings.
Prove termination over the declared parameter domain, including `(count + 1) / 2` under `count > 1` and the `count == 1` base case.
Reject nondecreasing recursion, missing base cases and unsupported cyclic construction with useful source diagnostics.
Preserve payload width/type, operation and bridge specialization identity; do not merge different operations because their default samples happen to match.
Allow multiple root counts/defaults to share the same definition where semantics match; distinguish default values from specialization identity.
Support real typed child connections and compiler body checks; do not replace recursion with an authored BlackBox or handwritten HDL.
Specify mutual recursion as a separate capability; either prove/support it explicitly or reject it clearly in the first release.
Retain arbitrary supported typed binary operations, including subtraction, signed arithmetic, bitwise operations and bundle-valued logic—not just unsigned sum.
Preserve adjacent-pair ordering and apply `levelBridge` to odd-tail lanes exactly as in the existing Spinal-style API.
Retain the existing concrete-`Int` bridge-level callback contract; specialize level-dependent callbacks internally rather than exposing manual per-level guards.
Diagnose unsupported captured parent signals or callback side effects rather than silently wiring across component ownership boundaries.
Keep `PIPELINE_MASK`: omitted/null removes built-in mask logic; an explicit zero keeps a parameterized combinational default; bit zero selects the first reduction stage.
Replace application-authored mask arithmetic with a concise library operation whose lowering preserves the current level numbering and legal domains.
Preserve callback-inserted registers and built-in mask registers without collapsing or duplicating latency; document their composition.
Infer/forward the current clock domain for ordinary single-domain child components, retaining explicit domains for CDC and genuine multi-domain boundaries.
Preserve asynchronous reset polarity, synchronous/soft reset priority, enable behavior and initial values through recursive and array-register lowering.
Emit `INITIAL_COUNT` or other level metadata only when needed; avoid unnecessary clock/pipeline scaffolding only where the public interface contract permits it.
Allow normal `child.io.input := parentValue` and `parentOutput := child.io.output` with symbolic aggregate widths, without mandatory `ModulePortWires` carriers.
Infer exact child-port geometry and direction evidence through intermediate expressions and whole-width slices.
Preserve meaningful explicit Scala names while marking compiler-generated plumbing anonymous; do not use application-specific names as cleanup rules.
Give parent-side child-port wires predictable names such as `event_source_up_data_out`; avoid adding helper implementation suffixes such as `Ports` by default.
Retain a user naming/keep mechanism for debug boundaries and attributes; do not remove intentionally named state or observable boundaries merely for appearance.
Keep generic Rust alias optimization for safe anonymous wires and proven simple combinational output aliases, with width, signedness, driver and generate-scope checks.
Emit consistent indentation, precedence-aware parentheses, stable generate labels and readable parameterized bounds in native output.
Share structurally identical component definitions; keep genuine behavioral/type specializations distinct and runtime enables as ports when authored that way.
Publish the qualified public syntax/API in MorphHDL with migration examples from each low-level construct.
Rewrite the balanced-tree library body using direct parameters, `if`, `for`, indexing and recursive construction; keep the existing convenient public `reduceBalancedTree` call.
Preserve operation-specific names such as `StatusCounterDeltaSum` and `StatusEventErrorUnion`; never require recursive/reduceBalancedTree wording in emitted module names.
Migrate representative CDC synchronizers/reset chains, multidimensional counter terms, CSR arrays and direct child-port connections.
Remove obsolete application proof/plumbing helpers only after all callers have qualified replacements; retain compatibility adapters for external callers where required.
Record library reuse decisions and avoid copying compiler algorithms into project RTL or introducing a second reduction algorithm.
Update application documentation, generation manifests and agreed compiler pins together after candidate qualification; do not silently move dependencies.
Freeze low-level baseline artifacts, source/compiler identities and expected behavior before migration.
Test native lightweight lowering before Rust cleanup, then independently validate cleaned RTL; cleanup must not conceal frontend errors.
Cover counts 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 15, 16 and supported 32/64 boundaries; cover widths 1, 8, 32, 36 and 64 and multidimensional geometries.
Cover unsigned/signed addition, non-associative subtraction, bitwise operations, bundles and level-dependent bridges.
Cover omitted masks, explicit zero and every legal mask for representative capacities; test reset, soft reset, enable stalls and odd-tail latency.
Override multiple parameters in the same emitted definition, including non-default child widths/counts and repeated roots with different defaults.
Run negative tests for invalid domains, width/signedness mismatches, unproven indices, overlapping writers, nonterminating recursion and illegal ownership.
Compare public-output traces against the frozen baseline, including X/Z-sensitive alias cases; use appropriate formal/equivalence checks for combinational transformations.
Regenerate twice and compare native and cleaned output hashes; verify expected arrays, generate loops, one shared recursive definition and absence of redundant carriers.
Run fresh lint and Questa unit tests with real children; bind bench geometry to the generation profile and reject port-width mismatches.
Run affected CDC/clock-stop, CSR, reduction and product integration suites; identify profiles not exercised rather than claiming all-profile qualification.
Verify downstream synthesis compatibility for the selected packed/unpacked dialect and confirm no unintended latches, storage or latency changes.
Publish exact commands, hashes, tool versions, result logs, limitations and rollback/migration instructions; close checkboxes only with corresponding evidence.
